name: NSW Blue Mountains Bushfire — Multi-Agency
description: A rapidly escalating bushfire in the Blue Mountains region west of Sydney requiring multi-agency coordination across fire, police, ambulance and SES. Exercises AIIMS activation, public warnings, evacuation planning and resource staging over an 8-hour period.

seed_organisations.name: New South Wales Rural Fire Service
Fire and Rescue New South Wales
New South Wales State Emergency Service

payload.summary: Severe fire weather warning: Catastrophic fire danger rating for Greater Sydney and Blue Mountains. Temperatures above 40°C, winds gusting 80 km/h, humidity below 10%.
Sentinel satellite hotspot detected near Wentworth Falls. Estimated fire area 2 ha.
Bush/grass fire reported. Wentworth Falls area. Fire not yet under control. ALERT level.
Field report: fire spreading rapidly NE under strong westerly winds. Spot fires reported ahead of main front. Estimated rate of spread 2 km/h.
Updated observations: Temperature 44°C, wind gusts to 95 km/h NW. Fire weather conditions deteriorating.
Fire upgraded to WATCH AND ACT. Fire area now 120 ha. Threatening Leura and Katoomba. Residents should enact bush fire survival plans.
Multiple social media reports of heavy smoke and ember attack in Leura. Residents posting evacuation photos.
AIIMS Level 2 declared. Multiple spot fires established NE of main front. Structure defence operations commencing in Leura.
Great Western Highway closed between Springwood and Lithgow due to fire activity. Blue Mountains Line rail services suspended.
EMERGENCY WARNING issued for Leura, Katoomba, Wentworth Falls. Fire area 450 ha. Too late to leave. Shelter in a solid structure.
Power outages affecting 12,000 customers in Blue Mountains LGA. Ausgrid crews unable to access affected substations.
AIIMS Level 3 declared. Fire area 800 ha. 15 structures confirmed lost. Request for interstate assistance lodged.
Satellite pass confirms fire perimeter spanning 1,200 ha. Active fire fronts on north and east flanks.
Blue Mountains Hospital reporting surge in smoke inhalation and heat-related presentations. 45 patients treated, 8 admissions.
Wind change to southerly. Fire behaviour moderating on southern flank. Northern flank still active. Containment operations commencing.
Community reports of fallen trees blocking evacuation routes on Cliff Drive, Leura. Multiple abandoned vehicles.
Southerly wind change fully established. Temperature dropping to 28°C. Relative humidity rising to 35%. Fire danger rating reducing.
Fire downgraded to WATCH AND ACT. Containment at 40%. Fire area 1,400 ha. 23 structures confirmed lost. Damage assessment teams deploying.
Containment operations progressing well. Back-burning successful on eastern flank. Containment at 55%.
Water supply pressure reduced in Katoomba and Leura due to firefighting demand. Water restrictions in effect for non-emergency use.
Fire downgraded to ADVICE. Containment at 70%. Fire area 1,500 ha. AIIMS Level 3 maintained. Recovery coordination planning initiated.

name: QLD Cyclone — Multi-Agency
description: A category 3 tropical cyclone making landfall near Cairns in Far North Queensland. Exercises cyclone tracking, progressive public warnings, evacuation of coastal communities, multi-agency coordination and post-landfall damage assessment over a 24-hour period.

payload.summary: Tropical Cyclone Watch issued for coastal areas between Cooktown and Innisfail. TC forming in Coral Sea, currently Category 1. Expected to intensify.
TC track forecast update: System intensifying, now Cat 2. Predicted landfall near Cairns in 18-22 hours. Peak gusts to 170 km/h expected.
Cyclone Warning UPGRADED. TC now Category 3. Destructive winds expected in coastal areas from Cooktown to Innisfail. Prepare to shelter.
Doppler radar tracking: eye wall visible. System maintaining Cat 3 intensity. Heavy rainfall bands extending 200 km from centre. Cairns radar reporting 100 mm/hr rainfall rates.
Pre-landfall: gale force winds now affecting Cairns CBD. Debris reported on streets. Power outages beginning in northern suburbs. All bridges closed.
QFES emergency situation declared for Cairns Regional Council area. All emergency services in shelter mode. No vehicle movements until wind gusts below 80 km/h.
TC has made landfall 20 km north of Cairns. Peak wind gusts 185 km/h recorded. Storm surge of 2.5 m above normal tide levels. Extreme rainfall continuing.
Major flood warning for Barron River at Cairns. River level 10.2 m (major flood level 9.4 m). Peak expected in 6 hours.
Social media surge: reports of roof damage in Cairns North, flooding in Smithfield. Unverified reports of building collapse on Sheridan St.
TC moving inland, weakening to Category 2. Destructive winds easing in coastal areas. Heavy rainfall continuing. Flash flooding risk remains very high.

Initial damage assessment: significant structural damage in Cairns North and Machans Beach. Multiple roads blocked by debris and fallen trees. Three evacuation centres active with 2,400 displaced residents.
Major infrastructure damage: Captain Cook Highway impassable. Bruce Highway blocked at Gordonvale. Cairns Airport closed. Rail services suspended north of Townsville.
Cairns Hospital operational on emergency generators. 87 storm-related presentations, 12 admissions, 3 critical. Pharmacy supplies for 72 hours.
Barron River peaked at 11.8 m (record flood). Slowly receding. Mulgrave River at 8.9 m (major flood). Flooding widespread across Cairns coastal plain.
Comprehensive damage assessment: 450 buildings damaged (85 severely), 12 km of power lines down, 8 major road closures remaining. Estimated 15,000 without power.
Air quality monitoring: asbestos risk identified in heavily damaged structures in Machans Beach. Exclusion zone recommended. EPA assessors mobilising.
TC weakened to tropical low. Gale warnings cancelled for coastal areas. Heavy rainfall warning continues for ranges. Flash flood risk remains.
AIIMS Level 2 maintained. Recovery coordination initiated. 5 evacuation centres operational (3,100 displaced). ADF asset request submitted. NEMA liaison en route.
Community Facebook groups: misinformation spreading about dam failure upstream. No dam failure confirmed. Cairns Regional Council issuing corrections.
Flood waters receding in Cairns coastal areas. SES conducting swift water rescue stand-down. 42 rescues completed during event. Road reopening assessments commencing.
ADF assets arrived: HMAS Choules en route, C-17 delivering emergency supplies to Cairns Airport (now operational for military flights). 200 ADF personnel deployed for debris clearance.
Recovery phase commencing. Power restored to 60% of affected areas. Bruce Highway reopened single-lane. Transition from response to recovery coordination underway.

24-hour situation report: TC dissipated. AIIMS Level 2 continuing. 3,100 displaced, 450 buildings damaged. Recovery plan being developed with all agencies. Community recovery hubs established at 3 locations.

name: NSW Hawkesbury-Nepean Riverine Flood
description: A major riverine flooding event in the Hawkesbury-Nepean valley west of Sydney, triggered by prolonged heavy rainfall. Exercises flood warning interpretation, progressive evacuation of low-lying communities, road closure management and inter-agency coordination over a 12-hour period.

seed_organisations.name: New South Wales State Emergency Service
Fire and Rescue New South Wales

payload.summary: Flood Watch for Hawkesbury-Nepean River system. Heavy rainfall forecast for catchment over next 24 hours. Minor flooding expected at Windsor and North Richmond.
Warragamba Dam spillway active. Inflows exceeding 100 GL/day. Rainfall intensity increasing in upper catchment. 80 mm recorded in last 6 hours.
Nepean River at Penrith: 8.2 m and rising (minor flood level 7.5 m). Rate of rise 0.4 m/hr. Peak forecast 12.5 m (major flood) in 8 hours.
Flood Warning UPGRADED to MAJOR for Hawkesbury River at Windsor. Expected to reach 13.0 m. Moderate flooding at North Richmond. Low-lying areas prepare to evacuate.
SES Evacuation ORDER issued for McGraths Hill, Cornwallis and Pitt Town Bottoms. 4,500 residents must evacuate immediately. Evacuation centres open at Richmond and Castle Hill.
Windsor Bridge closed. Hawkesbury River road crossings closed at Sackville, Wisemans Ferry. Richmond-Windsor road impassable. Only route via M7/M2 corridor.
Evacuation compliance estimated at 70%. SES door-knocking remaining residents in McGraths Hill. 15 requests for flood rescue assistance received. Marine Rescue boats deployed.
Hawkesbury at Windsor: 12.8 m and still rising. Rate of rise 0.5 m/hr. Revised peak forecast 14.5 m — exceeding 1 in 100 year level. Historic 1867 flood level 19.7 m.
EMERGENCY WARNING: Additional evacuation orders for Windsor CBD, South Windsor, Bligh Park. Total 18,000 residents under evacuation orders. This is a life-threatening emergency.

AIIMS Level 2 declared. Flood waters entering ground floors in South Windsor. 8 swift-water rescues completed. 2 people unaccounted for. Evacuation centres at capacity — opening additional centre at Rouse Hill.
Precautionary power shutdown in flood-affected areas. 22,000 customers without power across Hawkesbury LGA. Restoration dependent on flood recession.
Hawkesbury at Windsor peaked at 14.2 m. Now 14.0 m and slowly falling. Rate of fall 0.1 m/hr. Flood waters expected to remain above major flood level for 48+ hours.
Hawkesbury District Health Service: 23 flood-related presentations. 5 hypothermia cases. 2 people recovered from floodwaters — admitted ICU. Both unaccounted persons now located safe.
Rainfall easing across catchment. 6 mm recorded in last 3 hours (down from 30 mm/hr at peak). Clearing trend expected overnight. Catchment saturation remains extreme.
Situation stabilising. AIIMS Level 2 maintained. 14,200 evacuated (79% compliance). 4 evacuation centres active. Clean-up planning commenced. Road damage assessment scheduled for when waters recede.
North Richmond Water Filtration Plant offline due to extreme turbidity. Bottled water distribution organised for evacuation centres. Estimated 72 hours to restore treatment.
12-hour situation report: River at 13.5 m, falling slowly. All evacuated persons accounted for. No fatalities. Preliminary damage estimate 200+ properties inundated. Recovery coordinator appointed.

name: VIC/NSW Border Bushfire — Cross-jurisdiction
description: A large bushfire originating in north-east Victoria that crosses into southern NSW, triggering multi-state coordination, Commonwealth activation (COMDISPLAN) and ADF assistance. Exercises cross-jurisdictional AIIMS integration, resource sharing agreements, unified public messaging, and national-level escalation over a 48-hour period.

seed_organisations.name: New South Wales Rural Fire Service
New South Wales State Emergency Service

payload.summary: Extreme fire danger rating for North East Victoria and Southern Ranges NSW. Total fire ban declared both states. Temperatures 42°C+, winds NW 70 km/h.
Grass and scrub fire reported near Corryong, NE Victoria. CFA crews responding. Fire area approximately 10 ha. ALERT level.
Multiple satellite hotspots detected. Fire area estimated 80 ha. Rapid spread NE under strong winds. Spot fires detected 2 km ahead of main front.
WATCH AND ACT for Corryong and Cudgewa. Fire area 350 ha. Moving towards NSW border. AIIMS Level 2 declared VIC. Request for NSW RFS assistance submitted.
Fire has crossed Murray River into NSW near Bringenbrong. NSW RFS notified and responding. Dual-state AIIMS coordination being established. Fire area 800 ha total.
NSW RFS: WATCH AND ACT for Khancoban and Tooma areas. Fire established in Kosciuszko NP on NSW side. Separate AIIMS structure established NSW. Joint operations centre proposed.
EMERGENCY WARNING VIC: Corryong township under direct threat. Residents shelter immediately. Fire area 2,000 ha. 12 structures confirmed lost. AIIMS Level 3 declared.
EMERGENCY WARNING NSW: Khancoban and surrounding areas. Fire area on NSW side now 600 ha. Running through alpine country. Containment extremely difficult in terrain.

Joint State Operations Centre established in Wodonga. Unified command VIC/NSW agreed. Combined fire area 3,500 ha. 250 firefighters deployed (180 VIC, 70 NSW). Interstate resource sharing under mutual aid.
Overnight conditions: temperature dropped to 18°C, winds easing to 20 km/h. Humidity rising to 55%. Fire behaviour moderated significantly. Window for containment operations.
Overnight containment operations successful on southern and western flanks. 35% contained. Fire area 4,200 ha. Second hot day forecast — conditions expected to deteriorate by 1400.
NEMA activated COMDISPLAN. ADF assets requested: Black Hawk helicopters for water bombing, Army personnel for fire line construction. NEMA deploying liaison officers to Joint Operations Centre.
Himawari-9 satellite imagery shows massive smoke plume extending 300 km. Combined fire area estimated 6,500 ha across both states. New fire front developing in Kosciuszko NP.
AIIMS Level 3 declared NSW. Fire area NSW side 2,800 ha. Tumbarumba shire under EMERGENCY WARNING. National parks closed across Snowy Mountains region.

Major road closures: Murray Valley Highway closed Tallangatta to Corryong. Omeo Highway closed. Alpine Road closed. Hume Freeway traffic management in place at Wodonga. Cross-border movement restricted.

24-hour SITREP: Combined fire area 8,200 ha. 45% contained. 28 structures lost (VIC 18, NSW 10). 580 firefighters deployed including 120 ADF. 2 Black Hawk helicopters operational. Red Cross operating 4 relief centres.
Misinformation circulating on social media: false claims fire was deliberately lit. VicPol statement: cause under investigation, no evidence of arson. Corrective messaging issued.
Cool change moving through. SW winds 25 km/h, temperature 22°C, humidity 60%. Conditions favourable for containment over next 48 hours. No further hot days in 7-day outlook.
Containment progressing well. 65% contained. Cool conditions allowing aggressive back-burning. Fire area stable at 8,500 ha. Downgrading alerts for Corryong township.

Recovery transition planning commenced. Red Cross leading needs assessments. VIC: 18 structures lost, 350 livestock. NSW: 10 structures, 8,000 ha parkland. Recovery coordinators appointed both states.
Air quality: smoke haze reducing across NE VIC. PM2.5 levels returning to moderate (25-50 µg/m³). Health advisory for sensitive groups maintained.
Fire at 80% containment. Patrol and blacking-out operations continuing. AIIMS downgraded to Level 2 in both states. ADF draw-down commenced. Joint Operations Centre transitioning to recovery focus.

46-hour SITREP: 85% contained. Recovery operations ramping up. COMDISPLAN assistance continuing. National bushfire recovery agency briefed. Insurance assessors deployed. Community recovery meetings scheduled both sides of border.

48-hour final SITREP: Fire 90% contained, 8,600 ha. 28 structures lost, no fatalities. Full recovery coordination established. AIIMS to be stood down within 24 hours. Lessons learned capture process initiated.
